title: Layout: stacks, frames, alignment, spacers and GeometryReader

videos.script: In SwiftUI, no parent sets a child's size. {{steps}} The parent offers a size. The child chooses its own. Then the parent places it, and cannot change what the child chose. That one rule explains almost every surprise in layout. {{stacks}} Stacks share their space out. {{frames}} A frame is not a size you set. It is a new view, wrapped around the old one. {{align}} Alignment decides which edges, or which baselines, line up. {{spacer}} A spacer takes whatever is left, and padding adds space around a view. {{reader}} GeometryReader hands you the offer itself, and takes all the space it is given, which is why it is the last resort. {{model}} And then you run the arithmetic. About fifty lines of plain Swift that model how a stack serves its children. Least flexible first. You will see a title give way because it came last.
